Subject: Initial field mapping questions for Whistic profile

Hi David,

Thanks again for walking us through the Whistic flow earlier. We started reviewing the profile export and have a few areas where we need clarification so our security team can accept the submission as SOC2-aligned: 

- Field taxonomy: your export has a set of keys (contact_primary, org_summary, s3_evidence_link) that don't map 1:1 to our internal registry. Can you share recommended canonical mappings?
- Ephemeral creds: Somnus requires a short TTL for any demo/service account uploads. What examples do you have for presign/policy TTLs and how Redwood proves possession?
- Evidence retention: our audit wants the retention policy attached to each uploaded artifact (S3 presigned vs Drive link).

I've attached a CSV of our preferred canonical fields and a short spreadsheet with the temporary credential TTLs we permit. If you can reply with the mapping (or an updated CSV) by EOD tomorrow, we can move the Whistic profile to verified state.

Appreciate it —
Ava Reynolds
Director, IT Security
Somnus Health

Hi Ava —

Thanks for the clear list. Quick responses inline below and I attached a suggested mapping file (whistic_field_mapping_v1.csv) with our canonical keys plus notes about where evidence lives. High level:

- Contact fields: we map contact_primary -> org_profile.contact.name / org_profile.contact.email. We include phone only if provided.
- Artifact links: we prefer S3 presigned URLs for large logs; we include a signed-hash proof in the metadata so you can validate possession without downloading. See the presign examples doc.
- Ephemeral creds: standard demo/service accounts use presigned PUTs with a 1h TTL; for SOC2 evidence we recommend 15m TTL and a proof chain (signed upload manifest + CloudTrail event id).

Mina is looping in a short guide for Whistic-specific fields and the proof artifacts we attach in the metadata. Jonas is cc'd for the presign policy and retention SLAs. If that matches your audit needs, we'll stage the updated profile in Whistic and flag the CAIQ answers that reference the artifacts.

Next steps:
1) We'll upload the updated CSV to the Drive link you shared and attach the presign policy examples.
2) Mina will confirm the CloudTrail hash method (SHA256 chain) we use for evidence.
3) Jonas will follow up on retention windows for logs.

I'll send the Drive link shortly.

—David
David Kim

Hi Ava —

Following up with the implementation notes. A couple of technical clarifications for Somnus' auditors: 

1) Proof of possession: when we create a presigned PUT for evidence upload we record a signed manifest that contains: filename, content hash (sha256), upload timestamp, presign id, and the CloudTrail event id generated at object PUT. That manifest is stored in our KMS-backed evidence bucket and the manifest's signature is verifiable against our public key.

2) TTL and rotation: our internal policy defaults to 15m for evidence presigns; we can surface a 1h option for non-sensitive bulk transfers. Ephemeral service account keys are rotated automatically and the last rotation timestamp is available in the manifest metadata.

3) Whistic field mapping: we prefer canonical keys: org_profile.*, security_controls.sig.*, and evidence.manifests[]. In the attached CSV I've included the Whistic export name, our canonical name, and an example value for auditors.

If the auditors want a live demo of a presign upload + verification (manifest check -> CloudTrail lookup -> signature verification), we can run a 20-minute session later this week. Proposed times: Thu 2pm PT or Fri 11am PT.

Thanks — Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
